steps.title: Series and DataFrames
steps.body: A **Series** is a labeled column of values and a **DataFrame** is a table of Series. Select rows with a **boolean filter**, summarize with **groupby**, and tidy with **sort_values** and **fillna**.

steps.title: Building and filtering a DataFrame
steps.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"name": ["Ada", "Linus", "Grace"], "age": [36, 28, 45]})
print(df.shape)
print(df[df["age"] > 30]["name"].tolist())
print(round(df["age"].mean(), 1))

notes.text: A dict of columns becomes a table.
A boolean mask keeps only matching rows.
Column methods like mean summarize one column.

steps.title: groupby, aggregation and sorting
steps.code:
import pandas as pd

sales = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["A", "B", "A", "B"], "units": [5, 3, 7, 2]})
totals = sales.groupby("city")["units"].sum()
print(totals.to_dict())
print(sales.sort_values("units", ascending=False)["units"].tolist())
print(sales.groupby("city")["units"].agg(["min", "max"]).loc["A"].tolist())

notes.text: groupby splits rows by city and sum adds each group.
sort_values orders the rows by a column.
agg applies several summaries at once.

steps.title: Missing values and summary stats
steps.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

s = pd.Series([4.0, np.nan, 6.0, 10.0])
print(s.isna().sum())
print(s.fillna(0).tolist())
print(s.sum())
print(s.describe()["max"])

notes.text: isna flags missing values; sum counts the True flags.
describe gives count, mean, std, min, quartiles and max.

steps.title: Adding columns and reading CSV text
steps.code:
import io
import pandas as pd

raw = "item,qty,price\npen,4,1.5\nbook,2,12.0\n"
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(raw))
df["total"] = df["qty"] * df["price"]
print(df["total"].tolist())
print(df.loc[df["total"].idxmax(), "item"])

notes.text: read_csv builds a DataFrame from CSV text.
New columns are computed for every row at once.
idxmax finds the row label of the largest value.

steps.question: What does df.groupby('city')['units'].sum() return?
steps.explanation: groupby splits rows by city and sum adds up each group.

steps.question: What does this print?
steps.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
print(pd.Series([1, np.nan, 3]).isna().sum())
steps.explanation: Only one value is NaN, so isna().sum() is 1.

examples.title: Pandas: Series & DataFrame
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30], index=["a", "b", "c"])
print(s["b"])
print((s * 2).tolist())
df = pd.DataFrame({"name": ["Ada", "Linus"], "age": [36, 28]})

examples.title: Pandas: Filtering
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"name": ["Ada", "Linus", "Grace", "Alan"], "age": [36, 28, 45, 41], "city": ["UK", "FI", "US", "UK"]})
print(df[df["age"] > 35])
print(df[(df["city"] == "UK") & (df["age"] < 40)])
print(df[df["name"].isin(["Ada", "Alan"])]["age"].tolist())

examples.title: Pandas: groupby
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"team": ["red", "blue", "red", "blue", "red"], "points": [3, 5, 4, 1, 6]})
grouped = df.groupby("team")["points"]
print(grouped.sum())
print(grouped.mean())
print(grouped.count())

examples.title: Pandas: Aggregations
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"dept": ["A", "A", "B", "B"], "salary": [50, 60, 70, 90], "age": [30, 40, 35, 45]})
print(df.groupby("dept").agg({"salary": ["min", "max"], "age": "mean"}))
print(df[["salary", "age"]].sum())

examples.title: Pandas: Sorting
examples.description: Order rows by one or more columns.
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"name": ["Ada", "Linus", "Grace"], "score": [88, 95, 88]})
print(df.sort_values("score", ascending=False))
print(df.sort_values(["score", "name"]).reset_index(drop=True))

examples.title: Pandas: Missing Values
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1.0, np.nan, 3.0], "b": [np.nan, 5.0, 6.0]})
print(df.isna().sum())
print(df.fillna(0))
print(df.dropna())
print(df.fillna(df.mean()))

examples.title: Pandas: Summary Stats
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"hours": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], "score": [52, 58, 65, 70, 78], "group": ["x", "y", "x", "y", "x"]})
print(df[["hours", "score"]].describe().round(2))
print(round(df["hours"].corr(df["score"]), 3))
print(df["group"].value_counts().to_dict())
